recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant prose elsewhere; any cleanup of unlisted historical example files should be handled separately if those files are brought into build scope.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request for DSTU2 asking that CarePlan.activity.detail.prohibited be reworded because the old "Do NOT do" short/true-only definition made false ambiguous; the accepted resolution said true means must not engage in the activity and false means should engage in it.
initial_application: Commit bd9f60dbff updated the then-authoritative CarePlan spreadsheet definition to add the false interpretation. Related commit f39dde8e17 had already made the element optional with a false default, and later workflow-alignment history renamed prohibited to doNotPerform.
additional_context: CarePlan is active and approved in source/fhir.ini. Current source uses CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityDetail.doNotPerform, not the old prohibited name, and fhir.ini retains historical rename mappings for the old path. The current definition says false or missing means the activity should be engaged in and meaningWhenMissing repeats that interpretation. source/careplan/PFM.xml still contains the old prohibited element, but active CarePlan example/pack lists do not reference it.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and intentionally made no source edits because the build-scope CarePlan StructureDefinition already carries the resolved semantics and no active source input still presents the misleading old definition.

related_jiras.note: Made the same CarePlan modifier optional with false/missing semantics, explaining why FHIR-12171 needed an explicit false interpretation.
